items.reason: The bill changes the membership and chair of the Maryland Cybersecurity Council and tells it to work on cybersecurity threats from artificial intelligence and quantum computing. It has no frontier-model threshold and no duty on AI developers. It is a State advisory body on general cybersecurity, not a catastrophic-risk rule for advanced AI.

The bill is a 10 percent tax on AI computer processing that funds a displaced-worker transition fund, with record-keeping duties; it has no frontier threshold or catastrophic-risk aim and falls under the OUT-list item for workforce or economic measures.

The bill regulates high-risk AI systems used to make consequential decisions (credit, employment, housing and similar) and targets algorithmic discrimination. This falls under the OUT-list item for bills that only regulate AI use in one kind of decision. It has no frontier threshold and no catastrophic-harm provision.

The binding duties (9 V.S.A. §§ 2495d-2495f) apply to every 'inherently dangerous artificial intelligence system', defined to include any generative AI system or any high-risk system, so a small company's chatbot is covered. They are aimed at ordinary harms (consumer injury, discrimination, privacy, consequential decisions), not at catastrophic harm; the 10 billion parameter dual-use definition is only one limb of that broad class. This falls under the out-of-scope class of general duties on all AI systems and sector or decision-specific AI rules.
